description:
FOUND s438 (Opus 5) by the FIRST full-sweep run of the #472 PCL_DROP_LOG
instrument, in a RUN-TIME MODULE LOAD -- a population nothing could count
before: the system perl's own
lib/5.40.3/x86_64-linux/Devel/Peek.pm line 59, loaded by perl-tests/undef.t.

  $num |= (1<<index($D_flags, $_)) for split //, $on;   # Devel::Peek::debug_flags

REPRO, and the discriminator is WHITESPACE:

  my $n = (1<<index("ab","a"));    # PCL: statement dropped
  my $n = 1<<index("ab","a");      #      "Bug. Fell through. Missing case: ["
  my $n = (1<<length("ab"));       # same
  my $n = (1<<f("a"));             # same -- any call, not just a builtin
  my $n = (1 << index("ab","a"));  # LOWERS (spaces around <<)

PPI 1.291's token stream for the first line:

  Number     1
  HereDoc    <<index          <-- perl reads `<<` as left shift here
  Structure  (
  ...

perl's toke.c only starts a heredoc at `<<` where a TERM is expected; after a
complete term `1`, `<<` is the shift operator.  PPI applies the heredoc rule
whenever the `<<` is followed by an identifier character, so `1<<index(...)`,
`$x<<f()` and `2<<CONST` are all mis-lexed.  (`1<<2` is fine -- a digit is not
an identifier -- which is why this never showed up in arithmetic.)

LAYER: PPI upstream (rule 13).  The workaround is the `_repair_*` family in
Pl/Parser.pm, on the SAME discriminator #457 already built for `)-name`: the
previous significant token ENDS A TERM (`_ends_term`), so re-lex the HereDoc
token as Operator `<<` + the identifier that follows.  Watch the case it would
break: a real heredoc after a term-ending token does not exist in valid perl,
but `print $fh <<EOT` and `func <<EOT` DO (there `$fh`/`func` do not end a
term for this purpose) -- probe both before widening.

WHEN THE WORKAROUND LANDS: docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md gains its section and
docs/ppi-bug-report.t a failing row (rule 13, same commit).  Cost today: any
program that calls Devel::Peek::debug_flags dies at that line since the s435
flip; before the flip it silently computed nothing.
subject: PPI lexes `1<<index(...)` as a HEREDOC (`<<index`), so every unspaced left-shift by a CALL drops -- live in core Devel::Peek, found by the #472 child-drop instrument
